newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Mollov bank raises capital to 1.4 bln lvs.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Mollov bank raises capital to 1.4 bln lvs.

text.p: Bulgaria's private Mollov bank decided to raise capital to 1.4 billion levs from 800 million levs through a new share issue to meet higher minimum capital requirements, the bank's executive director said.
"The shareholders approved a capital rise to 1.4 billion levs," Nikolai Kalbov told reporters after an extraordinary shareholders' meeting.
Kalbov also said the meeting authorised the bank's board to negotiate merger options with other banks but declined to elaborate.
Mollov bank's registered capital is set at 800 million levs, of which 50 percent is covered by voting shares.

Last month the shareholders decided to change the bank's name to Compas Bank due to changes in its ownership after Mollov Financial Investment Group, controlled by Mollov bank owner, Valentin Mollov, transferred stakes to First Private Bank in July to cover outstanding debts.
The new name has yet to be approved by the central bank.

The central bank raised minimum capital requirements for banks in August to 1.4 billion levs for a domestic licence and 2.2 billion levs for a full one to bring capital-to-assets ratio of local banks closer to international standards.
The new requirements are to be met by March 31, 1997.
